whatThePageStates: The page is a catalogue of GuardDuty finding types that AWS has withdrawn. A short intro states plainly: "The following finding types are retired and no longer generated by GuardDuty", reinforced by an Important callout that says retired finding types cannot be reactivated. A Topics list names 21 finding types, and the body then gives one H2 section per finding type with a plain-English title, a default severity, an optional feature or data-source line, a description, and remediation advice. The only coverage assertion on the page is negative and uniform: every one of the 21 named finding types is explicitly NOT produced. The page makes no positive coverage claim of any kind, and says nothing about Regions, plans, or which resource types GuardDuty does cover.

features.featureName: Retired finding types (finding types GuardDuty no longer generates)
features.statuses: 0 Yes, 21 No, 0 Partial; 0+21+0=21. Every value on this page is an explicit NOT-supported. The negation is stated once, at the top, and inherited by the whole list: 'The following finding types are retired and no longer generated by GuardDuty', plus 'You can't reactivate retired GuardDuty finding types.' There is no per-row status column, no Yes/No cell, and no tri-state — the page is uniform. Counted three independent ways, all agreeing on 21: 21 bullets in the Topics list, 21 finding-type H2 sections (a 22nd H2, 'See also', is boilerplate and not a finding type), and 21 '**Default severity:**' lines. The 21 titles are all distinct.
features.scope: None for coverage purposes. Retirement is stated globally — not per-Region, not per-plan, not per-account-type. Three of the 21 sections carry a residual source annotation from when they were live (EKS audit logs on PrivilegeEscalation:Kubernetes/PrivilegedContainer and Persistence:Kubernetes/ContainerWithSensitiveMount; 'CloudTrail data events for S3' on Exfiltration:S3/ObjectRead.Unusual), and every section carries a default severity. Neither is a coverage scope: they are historical attributes of a finding that is no longer emitted, and they are present on only 3 of 21 rows, so they cannot form a second dimension.
features.reasoning: The unit of claim on this page is one GuardDuty finding type — the thing named in each Topics bullet and each H2, and the thing whose generation is being withdrawn. findingType is a catalogue axis because the list of GuardDuty finding types is published by GuardDuty about itself; it has no existence independent of the service. One section equals one finding type equals one axis value, so the row granularity and the axis granularity match exactly and nothing collapses. The claim direction matters more than the count here: this is a stated negative, which is a real coverage statement (unlike mere absence), and it must be recorded as 21 No, never as 21 supported items.

shouldNotExtract: The 'See also' section at the foot of the page — the Agent Toolkit for AWS / 'Skills for AI coding assistants' boilerplate and its `aws agent-toolkit search-skills` command — is nav and tooling advice, not coverage; it appears on every page in this guide. Also not coverage: the '**Topics**' heading itself and the anchor tags (<a name=...>); the default-severity values (Medium, High, Low) and the asterisked severity Notes about temporary credentials created on an instance, which are severity semantics, not support; the 'Remediation recommendations' paragraphs and their links (compromised-s3.md, compromised-creds.md, compromised-ec2.md, guardduty-remediate-kubernetes.md); the link to Document history for Amazon GuardDuty; the suppression-rule guidance and the resource.KubernetesDetails... field path; API names quoted as examples inside descriptions (CreateSecurityGroup, PutBucketPolicy, AttachUserPolicy, DescribeInstances, ListInstanceProfilesForRole, RunInstances, StopLogging, ListBuckets, ConsoleLogin) — these are illustrative prose, not an apiOperation coverage list; and the incidental service and resource names in prose (EC2, S3, IAM, EKS, CloudTrail, Kubernetes), which are not a service or resourceType enumeration.
coverageDimensions: REGION: nothing. The page never names a Region, a partition, or a Region availability note. Any per-Region figure attributed to this page is fabricated. SERVICE: nothing usable. Service names appear only inside finding-type identifiers and prose (EC2, S3, IAM, EKS/Kubernetes, CloudTrail); the page does not enumerate services and makes no per-service support claim, so deriving a service count from the finding-type prefixes would be an invented axis. RESOURCE TYPE: nothing. No resource-type list, no per-resource-type support statement. The single dimension this page actually supplies is a catalogue of 21 GuardDuty finding types, and the only thing it says about them is that they are retired — that is, explicitly NOT covered.
trap: The dominant trap is polarity: a parser that harvests headings or Topics bullets will pull 21 finding-type names and file them as GuardDuty's SUPPORTED finding types, inflating coverage by 21 and, worse, asserting support for detections AWS has explicitly withdrawn. The negation lives once, in an intro sentence and an Important callout, and is never repeated per row — so any row-local parser sees no 'No' and defaults to Yes. Runners-up: (1) counting 22 finding types by treating the 'See also' H2 as a section, or double-counting the 21 Topics bullets plus the 21 H2 sections to reach 42; (2) mistaking the three '**Feature:**' / '**Data source:**' lines for a dataSource coverage axis of size 3 when 18 rows carry no such line at all; (3) reading '**Default severity: Medium\*/High/Low**' or the asterisk Notes as a tri-state status column; (4) scraping the quoted API names from the descriptions as an apiOperation coverage list; (5) inferring a service or resourceType axis from the EC2/S3/IAM/Kubernetes prefixes in the finding-type names.
